title: Guided pin-and-rollback deprecation procedure for legacy model revisions
creator: Lina Park
description:
Scope: Define and implement a reproducible, low-friction deprecation workflow for older model revisions that balances customer notice, migration guidance, and safe rollback semantics. This ticket covers: policy, timeline templates, SDK/Console UX integration (pinning warnings and migration prompts), automated notice channels, performance-profile republishing strategy, and runbooks for rollbacks and emergency freezes.

Goals: 1) Provide clear, measurable steps for retiring model revisions while preserving customer control via version pinning. 2) Reduce user surprise by surfacing deprecation notices in Console, SDKs, and API responses. 3) Ensure safe rollbacks and automated fallbacks if a new default causes regressions. 4) Publish updated performance profiles for downstream model variants before sunset.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- 90% of affected customers see the deprecation notice within 48 hours of announcement (Console + email + SDK warnings).
- <= 5% of customers require emergency rollback by SRE after the first 30 days of sunset.
- Migration guide adoption: 60% of users pin or migrate to recommended variant within 30 days of first notice.

Stakeholders: PM (Lina Park), Eng leads (Mateo Alvarez, Priya Sengupta), Design (Rafael Kim), Docs (Maya O'Neill), SRE (Jordan Lee), Legal & Compliance (Anika Rao).

High-level timeline (recommended phased cadence):
1) Announcement phase (T0): Publish "Intent to Deprecate" blog + Console banner; mail to owners and workspace admins; post in customer Slack/CS channels. (T0 = date of public intent)
2) Guidance phase (T0 + 14 days): Publish migration guide + compatibility matrix, SDK warning release (beta), performance profile comparisons for recommended alternatives.
3) Soft-sunset / pinning grace (T0 + 30 days): Default routing shifts to recommended variant for non-pinned traffic; pinned customers continue to receive deprecated revision. Pinning APIs and Console pin flows are available; we surface explicit warnings when creating new pins.
4) Final-sunset (T0 + 90 days): Deprecated revision is removed from public default catalog and hosting; pinned customers receive a final forced-migration window and assisted migration options.

UX and API integration details:
- Console: banner flows for admins, workspace-level deprecation dashboard (count of requests by revision), migration checklist.
- SDKs: introduce a deprecation header in responses (X-Redwood-Deprecation: revision=rev1, until=2025-04-15, alternative=rev2); add opt-in verbose warnings in dev mode.
- API: return a deprecation object in model metadata endpoints; add a pinning API (PATCH /v1/apps/{app}/pins) that can be used by customers or our migration tool.

Performance profile publishing:
- Before T0 + 14d we must publish updated performance profiles for recommended alternatives (latency p50/p95, token/money cost, memory footprint, typical throughput) and attach representative workloads/evals. Links to the perf artifact should be included in the migration guide.

Rollbacks / emergency fallback policy:
- Rollback triggers: spike in error rate > 3x baseline OR customer-reported quality regression with high severity.
- Automatic fallback: traffic routing policy will fallback to last-known-good variant for the cohort if error budget is breached.
- Runbook: step-by-step rollback command list, contact list for cross-functional on-call, and postmortem template. Add runbook to Confluence and link in Console incident UI.

Migration tooling and incentives:
- One-click migrate in Console that creates a canary assignment to validate outputs before full switch.
- Migration helper: CLI tool that analyzes prompt set compatibility and suggests parameter changes (temperature, stop sequences) and recommended variant.
- Customer success program: outreach to top-100 consumers with migration assistance and potential credit for migration effort.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Soft-sunset duration: 30 vs 60 days (tradeoff between safety and operational cost). PM recommendation: 30 days for non-platform-critical revisions, 60 for major architecture changes.
- Whether to force-migrate pinned customers at final-sunset or to offer extended paid support window. Suggested: offer paid extended support with clear SLA and migration milestones.
